get.description:
Answers the latest audit events otoroshi keeps in its datastore, the most recent first: at most 1001 of them, the datastore itself keeping the `maxLogsSize` latest ones of the global configuration.

Each `filter.<field>=<value>` query parameter keeps the events whose top level `field` holds the value: a string equal to it, a boolean or a number equal to it once parsed, or an array holding it. `page` and `pageSize` give the page of the events the filters keep.

The events are answered as a json array, or as ndjson (one event per line) when the `Accept` header asks for `application/x-ndjson` and not for json. The call is itself audited (`ACCESS_AUDIT_EVENTS`). Super admins only.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to answer, starting at 1

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: The number of events of a page. Every event is answered when absent

200.description: The audit events, the most recent first: a json array, or one event per line with ndjson

400.description: The credentials are missing (the route that serves the admin api refuses the call before the controller runs), or `page` or `pageSize` is not a number

401.description: The credentials are wrong, or they do not give access to the admin api

403.description: The admin behind the credentials is not a super admin, or the backoffice user token of the `Otoroshi-BackOffice-User` header is invalid

429.description: The quotas of the credentials, or the number of calls allowed per ip address, are exceeded

get.summary: Read the live statistics of the whole traffic
get.description: Answers the counters of the whole traffic otoroshi handled (calls, bytes in and out), and the rates and average durations of the latest calls. Calling it is audited (`ACCESS_GLOBAL_LIVESTATS`). On a leader, the rates add up, and the durations average, the ones the members of the cluster report. The same as `GET /api/live/global`.

200.description: The live statistics of the whole traffic

400.description: The credentials are missing: the call carries no api key, and the route that serves the admin api refuses it before the controller runs

401.description: The credentials are wrong, or they do not give access to the admin api

403.description: The backoffice user token of the `Otoroshi-BackOffice-User` header is invalid

429.description: The quotas of the credentials, or the number of calls allowed per ip address, are exceeded

get.summary: Stream the metrics of the host
get.description: Answers a server sent events stream that sends, every 2 seconds and as long as the client keeps the connection open, the metrics of the jvm and of the host of the otoroshi instance that answers: cpu, heap, threads, and some environment variables. The `data` of each event is a json `HostMetrics`. Calling it is audited (`ACCESS_HOST_METRICS`).

200.description: A server sent events stream, an event every 2 seconds whose `data` is a json `HostMetrics`

400.description: The credentials are missing: the call carries no api key, and the route that serves the admin api refuses it before the controller runs

401.description: The credentials are wrong, or they do not give access to the admin api

403.description: The backoffice user token of the `Otoroshi-BackOffice-User` header is invalid

429.description: The quotas of the credentials, or the number of calls allowed per ip address, are exceeded

get.summary: Read the live statistics of a route
get.description: Answers the counters of the traffic of a route (calls, bytes in and out), and the rates and average durations of its latest calls. With `every`, answers a server sent events stream that sends them every `every` milliseconds, as long as the client keeps the connection open, the `data` of each event being a json `LiveStats`. Calling it is audited (`ACCESS_SERVICE_LIVESTATS`). On a leader, the rates add up, and the durations average, the ones the members of the cluster report. The number of requests being handled right now is the one of the whole instance (or cluster), not of the route.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The id of the route, or `global` for the whole traffic. The ids of apis, of their routes, of route compositions and of drafts are accepted too

parameters.name: every
parameters.description: Answers a server sent events stream that sends the statistics every `every` milliseconds instead of a single json document

200.description: The live statistics: a json document, or with `every` a server sent events stream whose events hold a json `LiveStats` in their `data`

400.description: The credentials are missing, or `every` is not an integer

401.description: The credentials are wrong, or they do not give access to the admin api

403.description: The credentials cannot read the entity

429.description: The quotas of the credentials, or the number of calls allowed per ip address, are exceeded

get.summary: Read the statistics of the whole traffic over a period
get.description: Answers the statistics of every call of the period, read from the Elasticsearch cluster of the global configuration (`elasticReadsConfig`): counts, bytes, durations and overheads, their histograms over time, and the calls by status code and by route. Calling it is audited (`ACCESS_GLOBAL_STATS`). Super admins only.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The start of the period, as a unix timestamp in milliseconds. The whole history when absent

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: The end of the period, as a unix timestamp in milliseconds. Now when absent

200.description: The statistics of every call of the period, the calls by route included

400.description: The credentials are missing (the route that serves the admin api refuses the call before the controller runs), `page` or `pageSize` is not a number, or `from` or `to` is not a timestamp in milliseconds

401.description: The credentials are wrong, or they do not give access to the admin api

403.description: The admin behind the credentials is not a super admin, or the backoffice user token of the `Otoroshi-BackOffice-User` header is invalid

404.description: The global configuration has no Elasticsearch cluster to read the analytics from (`elasticReadsConfig`)

429.description: The quotas of the credentials, or the number of calls allowed per ip address, are exceeded

500.description: The Elasticsearch cluster does not work, cannot be reached, or failed to answer

get.summary: Read the statistics of a route, an api key or a group over a period
get.description: Answers the statistics of the calls of the period made to a route (`service`), with an api key (`apikey`) or to the routes of a group (`group`), read from the Elasticsearch cluster of the global configuration (`elasticReadsConfig`): counts, bytes, durations and overheads, their histograms over time, and the calls by status code (and by route, for an api key or a group). `fields` keeps only some of them.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The start of the period, as a unix timestamp in milliseconds. The whole history when absent

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: The end of the period, as a unix timestamp in milliseconds. Now when absent

parameters.name: service
parameters.description: The id of the route whose statistics are read. Takes precedence over `apikey` and `group`

parameters.name: apikey
parameters.description: The client id of the api key whose statistics are read. Takes precedence over `group`

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: The id of the group of routes whose statistics are read

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Comma separated list of the statistics to answer, among `statusesPiechart`, `statusesHistogram`, `overheadPercentiles`, `overheadStats`, `durationPercentiles`, `durationStats`, `dataInStats`, `dataOutStats`, `hits`, `dataIn`, `dataOut`, `avgDuration`, `avgOverhead` and `servicePiechart` (case insensitive). All of them when absent

200.description: The statistics of the calls of the route, the api key or the group (named in `type`), only the ones of `fields` when it is given

400.description: The credentials are missing (the route that serves the admin api refuses the call before the controller runs), `page` or `pageSize` is not a number, or `from` or `to` is not a timestamp in milliseconds

401.description: The credentials are wrong, or they do not give access to the admin api

403.description: The credentials cannot read the route, the api key or the group

404.description: The global configuration has no Elasticsearch cluster to read the analytics from (`elasticReadsConfig`), none of `service`, `apikey` and `group` is given, or the entity they name does not exist

429.description: The quotas of the credentials, or the number of calls allowed per ip address, are exceeded

500.description: The Elasticsearch cluster does not work, cannot be reached, or failed to answer

get.summary: Read the health of the routes over a period
get.description: Answers the health of the routes the credentials can read whose health check is enabled, day by day, read from the health check events of the Elasticsearch cluster of the global configuration (`elasticReadsConfig`). The routes are sorted by name and paginated: the `X-Count` header holds the number of routes, `X-Offset`, `X-Page` and `X-Page-Size` the page answered. Calling it is audited (`ACCESS_GLOBAL_STATUSES`).

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The start of the period, as a unix timestamp in milliseconds. 90 days ago, at the start of the day, when absent

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: The end of the period, as a unix timestamp in milliseconds. Now when absent

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page of routes to answer: the page answered starts at the route `page * pageSize` (counted from 0)

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: The number of routes of a page. Every route when absent

200.description: The health of the routes, the ones with no health check event left out

X-Count.description: The number of routes the credentials can read whose health check is enabled

X-Offset.description: The position of the first route of the page

X-Page-Size.description: The number of routes of a page

400.description: The credentials are missing (the route that serves the admin api refuses the call before the controller runs), `page` or `pageSize` is not a number, or `from` or `to` is not a timestamp in milliseconds

401.description: The credentials are wrong, or they do not give access to the admin api

404.description: The global configuration has no Elasticsearch cluster to read the analytics from (`elasticReadsConfig`), or no route the credentials can read has its health check enabled

429.description: The quotas of the credentials, or the number of calls allowed per ip address, are exceeded

500.description: The Elasticsearch cluster does not work, cannot be reached, or failed to answer

post.summary: Read the health of some routes over a period
post.description: Answers the health of the routes listed in the body (every route when the body is not an array) that the credentials can read, day by day, read from the health check events of the Elasticsearch cluster of the global configuration (`elasticReadsConfig`).

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The start of the period, as a unix timestamp in milliseconds. 90 days ago, at the start of the day, when absent

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: The end of the period, as a unix timestamp in milliseconds. Now when absent

requestBody.description: The ids of the routes whose health is read. Any other json value than an array reads the health of every route

200.description: The health of the routes, the ones with no health check event left out

400.description: The credentials are missing, or the body is not valid json

401.description: The credentials are wrong, or they do not give access to the admin api

404.description: The global configuration has no Elasticsearch cluster to read the analytics from (`elasticReadsConfig`), or none of the routes exists or can be read by the credentials

415.description: The body is not sent as `application/json`

429.description: The quotas of the credentials, or the number of calls allowed per ip address, are exceeded

500.description: The Elasticsearch cluster does not work, cannot be reached, or failed to answer

get.summary: List the gateway events of a route, an api key or a group
get.description: Answers a page of the gateway events of the period, read from the Elasticsearch cluster of the global configuration (`elasticReadsConfig`): the calls made to a route (`service`), with an api key (`apikey`), or to the routes of a group (`group`). Without any of them, every call of every tenant (organization) is answered, to super admins only.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The start of the period, as a unix timestamp in milliseconds. The whole history when absent

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: The end of the period, as a unix timestamp in milliseconds. Now when absent

parameters.name: service
parameters.description: The id of the route whose gateway events are read. Takes precedence over `apikey` and `group`

parameters.name: apikey
parameters.description: The client id of the api key whose gateway events are read. Takes precedence over `group`

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: The id of the group of routes whose gateway events are read

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: The order of the events, by date

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: The page to answer, starting at 1

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: The number of events of a page

200.description: A page of the gateway events of the route, the api key or the group, or of the whole traffic, with what they are filtered on in `type`

400.description: The credentials are missing (the route that serves the admin api refuses the call before the controller runs), `page` or `pageSize` is not a number, or `from` or `to` is not a timestamp in milliseconds

401.description: The credentials are wrong, or they do not give access to the admin api

403.description: The credentials cannot read the route, the api key or the group, or none of them is given and the admin behind the credentials is not a super admin

404.description: The global configuration has no Elasticsearch cluster to read the analytics from (`elasticReadsConfig`), or the route, the api key or the group does not exist

429.description: The quotas of the credentials, or the number of calls allowed per ip address, are exceeded

500.description: The Elasticsearch cluster does not work, cannot be reached, or failed to answer

get.summary: List the fields of a kind of event
get.description: Answers the paths of the fields of a kind of event, sorted, the fields of the nested objects written with dots (`data.dataIn`). They are read from the Scala class of the event, the names of its fields as they are written in its json (`@id`, `@timestamp`). The backoffice suggests them in the filters and the projections of the data exporters.

parameters.name: eventType
parameters.description: The kind of event whose fields are listed: the name of its Scala class, like `GatewayEvent`, `HealthCheckEvent` or `AdminLoggedInAlert`

200.description: The paths of the fields of the event

items.description: The path of a field, the names of the nested fields separated by dots

400.description: The credentials or `eventType` are missing, or `eventType` is not a known kind of event (answered in plain text)

401.description: The credentials are wrong, or they do not give access to the admin api

403.description: The backoffice user token of the `Otoroshi-BackOffice-User` header is invalid

429.description: The quotas of the credentials, or the number of calls allowed per ip address, are exceeded

get.summary: Stream the events of the node
get.description: Answers a server sent events stream of the events the otoroshi instance that answers produces (gateway events, audit and alert events, health checks, jobs...), as long as the client keeps the connection open. The `data` of each event is the json of an otoroshi event. Only the events produced after the connection are sent, and only those of this instance, not of the other members of the cluster. The stream stays empty when `otoroshi.options.useEventStreamForScriptEvents` is `false`. Super admins only.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: Only sends the events of this `@type`

200.description: A server sent events stream, an event per otoroshi event whose `data` is its json

schema.description: The json of an otoroshi event: its `@id`, `@timestamp`, `@type` and the fields of its kind

400.description: The credentials are missing: the call carries no api key, and the route that serves the admin api refuses it before the controller runs

401.description: The credentials are wrong, or they do not give access to the admin api

403.description: The admin behind the credentials is not a super admin, or the backoffice user token of the `Otoroshi-BackOffice-User` header is invalid

429.description: The quotas of the credentials, or the number of calls allowed per ip address, are exceeded
